text: Most code generation starts with a prompt. Our workflow starts with real enterprise governance context.
A Coding Agent reads DataHub through MCP and generates TeaQL applications inside a controlled network.
This is the real payment_transactions dataset running in our DataHub instance.
Its schema exposes four business fields and marks payment_account as PII.
The Agent maps each field into TeaQL and turns governance policy into _audit_mask_fields.
Zero upstream lineage means the model does not invent a payment-to-user relationship.
The generator runs on 127.0.0.1. The model never leaves the controlled network.
Java and Rust are generated from empty directories, then verified for deterministic output.
Raw audit events stay on a controlled forensic path. Analytics receive only SafeAuditEvent.
Real Java and Rust tests prove that payment_account is masked before safe output.
When DataHub returns entity not found, the Agent refuses to invent fields or relationships.
Enterprise DataHub governance now constrains the model, generated code, and runtime behavior.
